methodologyNotes: Covers E-Ink writing tablets: electronic-paper devices built around a pen/stylus for handwriting and notetaking (as distinct from pocket e-readers meant only for reading), sold at a published US price. Includes dedicated note-takers (reMarkable, Supernote), note-capable e-readers with an active pen (Kindle Scribe, Kobo Elipsa), and Android E-Ink tablets (Onyx Boox, Bigme). Excludes reading-only e-readers with no pen input (basic Kindle/Kobo), LCD 'boogie board' writing slates, and standard backlit tablets. Price is typical US MSRP or street price, USD, for the base storage configuration named. screenSizeIn is the E-Ink display's diagonal size in inches. ppi is the display's pixel density in pixels-per-inch (the monochrome/black-and-white layer's ppi where a device has a separate lower-resolution color layer). storageGb is the internal storage in gigabytes for the configuration priced. colorDisplay is a boolean: true if the panel renders color E-Ink (e.g. Kaleido/Gallery), false if monochrome. frontLight is a boolean for a built-in front light (any front light counts, warm or white). penIncluded is a boolean: true if a stylus/pen ships in the box at the listed price, false if the pen is sold separately. waterproof is a boolean for an official IP water-resistance rating. batteryWeeks is the manufacturer's stated typical battery life in weeks. Any spec not stated verbatim on a fetched manufacturer or retailer/review page is left null.

products.name: reMarkable Paper Pro
products.priceNote: Official reMarkable US buyer's-guide/shop page lists the reMarkable Paper Pro base configuration at "From $629" with "Marker included" (accessed 2026-07-11). The independent eWritable review notes the device-only launch price was "Starting at $579" (2024); the $629 figure reflects the current Marker-included base price.
products.provenance: The official reMarkable shop page (source) lists "reMarkable Paper Pro ... From $629 ... Marker included," confirms the 11.8" Canvas Color display and adjustable reading light, and identifies it as the largest "Paper Pro" model — distinct from the 10.3" black-and-white Paper Pure and the smaller Paper Pro Move (model-identity check passed). The eWritable review (corroboration, published Oct 9 2024) confirms the same model: 11.8" Gallery3 color panel, "229PPI ... for monochrome," "64Gb of storage," release year 2024, and an independent launch price "Starting at $579." Battery life in weeks and a warm/color-temperature reading light were not stated for the Pro on either cited page (the reviewer measured ~2.6 days and disputes the marketing claim), so both are left null.

products.name: reMarkable 2
products.priceNote: Standalone tablet starting price $279 per Tom's Guide review (tomsguide.com/reviews/remarkable-2-review): "available for purchase from the company's website at a price starting at $279"; Marker ($49) and Folio ($69) sold separately. At launch it was sold in a $399 bundle that included the Marker, Folio and express shipping. The manufacturer page lists no price since the model is discontinued.
products.provenance: Confirmed the exact model on reMarkable's official en-US product page (title "reMarkable 2 paper tablet (Discontinued - See reMarkable Paper Pure)"), whose Tech Specs list the full hardware verbatim: 10.3" monochrome Second-generation CANVAS display, 1872 x 1404 (226 PPI), Partially powered by E Ink Carta; 1.2 GHz dual core ARM; 1 GB LPDDR3 SDRAM + 8 GB internal storage; 3000 mAh Li-ion; 187 x 246 x 4.7 mm, Approximately 403.5 g; Wi-Fi 2.4GHz and 5 GHz + USB-C; reMarkable OS (Linux-based). Tom's Guide's dated reMarkable 2 review corroborates the same CPU/storage/RAM/display specs and is the price source: standalone tablet "starting at $279" (Marker and Folio sold separately), with a $399 launch bundle noted. Release year 2020 is stated on Tom's Guide ("Introducing reMarkable 2 — the paper tablet (2020)"); the manufacturer page carries no standalone price because the model is now discontinued.

products.name: Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024)
products.priceNote: Base 16 GB model. Tom's Guide "Kindle Scribe (2024) review" shows "$399.99" as the retail price in its deals widget and states a "starting price of $399 for the 16GB model" (32GB $419, 64GB $449). The Amazon manufacturer product page did not render a numeric price (the comparison-table PRICE row showed "-").
products.provenance: Amazon's official Kindle Scribe product page (source, "Kindle Scribe with redesigned display" column) confirms the exact 2024 model: a 10.2" glare-free 300 ppi display, "16 GB, 32 GB, or 64 GB" storage (16 GB base config), battery "Up to 12 weeks", "16-level gray scale" (monochrome, no color panel), and "Yes. Premium Pen included." — but its comparison-table PRICE, warm-light and waterproof cells rendered as blanks/checkmark icons. Tom's Guide's "Kindle Scribe (2024) review" (corroboration, dated 4 December 2024) verifies the same 10.2-inch 300 PPI display and 16GB storage, plus the specs "Front light: Adjustable warm light", "Battery life: Up to 12 weeks", the con "Not waterproof", and the price ("$399.99" in its deals widget; "starting price of $399 for the 16GB model"). Model identity is the 2nd-generation 2024 Scribe (not the 2022 original): both pages use the "(2024)"/"redesigned" naming and bundle the new color-matched Premium Pen, and Good e-Reader independently states "In late 2024, it released the Kindle Scribe 2" with a "10.2-inch ... 300 PPI" display.

products.name: Kobo Elipsa 2E

products.provenance: Schema note: the named e-ink-tablets.json does not exist in the repo; specKeys and methodology were taken from data/products/e-readers.json, which already holds the sibling Boox Note Air4 C. The official BOOX store product page (shop.boox.com/products/noteair5c) confirmed verbatim the 10.3" Kaleido 3 (4,096-color) screen at B/W 2480 x 1860 (300 ppi), 6 GB RAM / 64 GB ROM, Android 15, a "Front Light with CTM (Warm and Cold)" (warm_light=true), a 3,700 mAh Li-ion Polymer battery, and the BOOX Pen3 stylus listed in "Included In The Box (standard only)" (stylus_included=true); the only button in the hardware spec is the "Power Button with Fingerprint Recognition" and no IP water rating is listed anywhere, so page_turn_buttons=false and waterproof=false. That page's comparison table lists the Note Air5 C at "$499.99 Order Now" (vs. Note Air4 C $469.99 and Tab X C $759.99), giving the price. The Wikipedia Onyx Boox device table corroborates the exact Note Air5 C row — October 2025 launch, Android 15, Snapdragon 690, 6 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, 10.3" (2480×1860) Kaleido 3, predecessor Note Air4 C — confirming model identity as the Note Air5 C (not the Note Air4 C or Tab X C).
